q: Define and explain Economics as given by Professor Marshall and Robbins, which one do you consider better?
a: Answers: Definitions of Economics: Professor Marshall’s Definition of Economics: “Economics is a study of mankind in the ordinary business of life: it enquires how he gets his income and how he uses it. Thus it is on one side a study of wealth and on the other, and more important side, a part of the study of man." Professor Robbins’ Definition of Economics: "Economics studies human behavior as a relationship between ends and scarce means which have alternative uses." Comparison of Marshall’s and Robbins’ Definition: Marshall’s definition states that Economics is closely related to our ordinary business of life. It discusses our economic problems, individually, as well as, collectively. We examine, moreover, our efforts made for the material welfare and well-being of our life. In short, we can say that Economics is related to our ordinary economic problems and that how can we attain prosperity by material requisites. Professor Alfred Marshall determines the subject matter of Economics as, "The individual and collective human efforts to produce material requisites for human welfare and well-being." Professor Lionel Robbins is of the opinion that the purpose of Economic motive is to satisfy unlimited human wants by limited means. He further proposes that man should follow a certain line of action to satisfy his unlimited wants by his scarce means. Thus, preferring and satisfying the most important want first, he can be able to solve many of his economic problems gradually. The Best Definition:

q: Define Economics and describe the advantages (Utility) of the study of Economics?
a: Answers: Definition of Economics: "Economics studies human behavior as a relationship between ends and scarce means which have alternative uses." Importance and Advantages (Utility) of Study of Economics: Economics has both, theoretical and practical aspects regard to its importance and usefulness. It is not only useful from the individual point of view but it is also useful from the social standpoint. The study of economics has the greatest utility for the individual. He acts in our society under different conditions and circumstances and in different capabilities. He is a householder, a businessman, a laborer, a politician, and a reformer. To a householder, economics teaches the method of adjusting his expenditure within his limited income, so that he may get great satisfaction Out of It tells how he plans his expenditure on necessaries, comforts, and luxuries when the income of a man increases. A businessman can make use of this science in order to raise the margin of profit in his business, Internal and external economies can be affected and greater profits can be earned by reducing the prices of goods. The laborers can also get equal benefits with the study of economics. It tells him the ways of earning high wages i.e. the method by which he can raise his standard of living. If any political leader or Government official learns economics, he can help the State and can also bring prosperity to the people of the country. The state can reduce its unnecessary expenditure. He can suggest the ways ahead method of improving the standard of fiving. The finances of the country can also be improved by solving the monetary difficulties. Social evils are found in the society where large-scale production is taken up because of the extent of the market. Social reformers can take this aspect of economic life and can remove the evils which are chiefly due to economic causes. He cannot do away with them unless he studies economics. Thus Economic Science is useful in theory and practice for all the people inhabited a particular country.

q: What do you mean by the nature of the Economic problem?
a: How does an Economic problem arise? How it can be solved by an individual or by State Economists (authorities)? Answers: Economic Problem Problems which is related to the unlimited human wants against human scare means to satisfy them, is called Economic Problem. Nature of Economic Problem Human wants are unlimited. Means are scarce. How to satisfy unlimited from scared means. We know the fact that our wants are unlimited in number and that they remain existing continuously for our whole life. We possibly cannot satisfy them all. Sometimes we feel thirst and hunger; sometimes we want clothing and conveyance, when we satisfy these wants, the other wants exist continuously, which follow us up to the end of our life. Thus the economic problem exists due to unlimited wants. We follow a particular line of action to solve it because of our scarce means. The phrase "scarce means" does not mean that there is a vast shortage of goods and services in the world. It is not so, at all, because we produce many million tons of crops, millions of yards of cloth, millions of cars and scooters, and all the necessities of life. Solution of Economic Problem: The Economic problems differ according to the conditions of an economy. They keep changing their state, always. It is the first and foremost duty of an Economist to pay full attention to solve these problems in accordance with the economic condition and resources of the society. It is necessary to assess and determine the economic resources versus economic problems.
